title: Digital SAT Reading and Writing — Full-Length Original Practice
description: Unofficial original practice: 54 questions in two 27-question modules, 32 minutes each (64 minutes total). Not an official SAT or scaled score.

sat.instructions: Complete both 27-question modules. This is unofficial practice and does not produce an official SAT scaled score.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A survey of 240 city residents found that 156 used the riverside path at least once a week. Which choice gives the percentage?

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: Researchers compared two wetlands. Site A had 18 bird species in spring and 26 in autumn; Site B had 22 in spring and 24 in autumn. Which statement is supported?
options: Site A had more species in both seasons.
Site B had the larger seasonal increase.
Site A had the larger seasonal increase.
Both sites had the same autumn count.
questions.correctAnswer: Site A had the larger seasonal increase.
questions.explanation: Site A increased by 8; Site B increased by 2.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A historian notes that the first public timetable for the North Line appeared in 1908, two years after the line opened. What does the evidence establish?
options: The timetable came after the line opened.
questions.correctAnswer: The timetable came after the line opened.
questions.explanation: The dates establish sequence, not ownership or universal compliance.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A study found that seedlings under blue filters grew 12 cm on average, while those under clear filters grew 15 cm. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Blue light prevents all plant growth.
The clear-filter group grew 3 cm more on average.
questions.correctAnswer: The clear-filter group grew 3 cm more on average.
questions.explanation: The group means differ by 3 cm; the data alone do not prove causation.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A museum labels an object as probably made near the coast because its clay contains a mineral common in coastal deposits. What is the role of the mineral evidence?
options: It supports a cautious origin hypothesis.
questions.correctAnswer: It supports a cautious origin hypothesis.
questions.explanation: The wording “probably” signals evidence for an inference, not proof.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A town planted 40 trees in Year 1 and 52 in Year 2. What was the percent increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 12; 12 ÷ 40 = 0.30.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: An archive contains 320 letters. Of these, 80 mention the harbour and 48 mention the market. If 20 mention both, how many mention at least one?
questions.explanation: Use inclusion-exclusion: 80 + 48 − 20 = 108.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A botanist measured leaf width in shade and sun. The median was 6.2 cm in shade and 4.8 cm in sun. Which comparison is valid?
options: The shade median was 1.4 cm greater.
The sun leaves had no variation.
The mean shade width was 6.2 cm.
questions.correctAnswer: The shade median was 1.4 cm greater.
questions.explanation: Subtracting the medians gives 1.4 cm; medians do not describe every leaf or the mean.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A report says a new bus route carried 900 riders in its first week and 1,170 in its fourth week. Assuming the same weekly increase, what was the average increase per week?
questions.explanation: There are three week-to-week intervals: (1,170 − 900) ÷ 3 = 90.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A researcher tested a new study app with volunteers who chose to use it. Which limitation matters most?
options: The sample may not represent all students.
The volunteers were assigned at random.
questions.correctAnswer: The sample may not represent all students.
questions.explanation: Self-selection can limit how broadly findings generalize.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A map shows the old canal 4 km east of the station and the new footbridge 1.5 km west of the canal. How far is the bridge east of the station?
questions.correctAnswer: 2.5 km

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: An experiment randomly assigned 60 participants to use either a paper planner or a digital planner. What feature most strengthens a causal comparison?
options: Random assignment to the two conditions
The use of two planner types
A larger font in one planner
questions.correctAnswer: Random assignment to the two conditions
questions.explanation: Random assignment helps balance other differences between groups.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A collection grew from 1,200 items to 1,500 items. What fraction of the original collection was added?
questions.explanation: 300 items were added; 300/1,200 = 1/4.

questions.satSkill: Central ideas, details, and quantitative evidence
questions.text: A scientist reports that a result was not statistically significant. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: The study proved there is no effect.
The data did not provide strong evidence against the null model.
questions.correctAnswer: The data did not provide strong evidence against the null model.
questions.explanation: A non-significant finding is not proof of no effect.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: In the sentence ‘The proposal met with a cool reception,’ cool most nearly means
questions.correctAnswer: calm and reserved
questions.explanation: The phrase describes an unenthusiastic response.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A writer describes a bridge as ‘a patient instrument, measuring each passing season.’ The phrase primarily suggests that the bridge
questions.correctAnswer: records gradual environmental change
questions.explanation: The metaphor links the bridge’s endurance with observation over time.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: Text 1 argues that city roofs should be gardens because they cool buildings. Text 2 agrees about cooling but says roofs must first be checked for load capacity. How does Text 2 relate to Text 1?
options: It changes the topic to transport.
It supplies proof that gardens are harmful.
questions.correctAnswer: It adds a practical qualification.
questions.explanation: Text 2 accepts the benefit but conditions implementation.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A paragraph begins, ‘The first trial was modest, but it changed the debate.’ What is the function of this sentence?
options: It introduces a contrast and signals significance.
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces a contrast and signals significance.
questions.explanation: “But” contrasts the trial’s scale with its influence.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: In a passage about restoring a marsh, ‘the intervention’ refers to
options: the deliberate restoration work described earlier
questions.correctAnswer: the deliberate restoration work described earlier
questions.explanation: The phrase points back to the restoration action.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A poet calls a schedule ‘a map that leaves room for weather.’ The metaphor emphasizes that a schedule should
questions.correctAnswer: allow for unexpected changes
questions.explanation: The image presents planning as flexible rather than rigid.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A study’s authors write that the result is ‘suggestive rather than conclusive.’ This wording indicates that the evidence is
questions.correctAnswer: promising but not definitive
questions.explanation: “Suggestive” signals an indication, while “not conclusive” limits certainty.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: Text 1 says local archives preserve details absent from national histories. Text 2 argues that archives also need shared cataloguing standards. Text 2 mainly
options: extends the discussion with a condition for access
repeats the same point without change
argues that national history is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: extends the discussion with a condition for access
questions.explanation: It adds a practical point about making archives discoverable.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A researcher writes, ‘The apparent decline is an artefact of the new counting method.’ Here artefact most nearly means
questions.correctAnswer: a misleading effect of measurement
questions.explanation: The counting method creates an appearance that may not reflect a real decline.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A passage first describes a failed prototype, then a revised one that worked. Why include the first prototype?
options: To show how the later design addressed a problem
To prove the goal was abandoned
questions.correctAnswer: To show how the later design addressed a problem
questions.explanation: The sequence reveals what changed between attempts.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: A historian calls a decree ‘an imperfect compromise.’ The adjective imperfect most nearly conveys that the decree
options: resolved some disputes but left others
questions.correctAnswer: resolved some disputes but left others
questions.explanation: A compromise can settle part of a disagreement without satisfying everyone.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: Text 1 presents a mural as a record of neighbourhood history. Text 2 focuses on how residents choose its imagery. The two texts differ mainly in their emphasis on
options: the mural’s historical function versus its creation process
the cost of paint versus the cost of stone
questions.correctAnswer: the mural’s historical function versus its creation process
questions.explanation: Text 1 discusses what the mural records; Text 2 discusses how it is made.

questions.satSkill: Words in context and text structure
questions.text: In a passage, a ‘narrow window’ of favourable conditions refers to
options: a limited period when conditions are suitable
a small opening in a wall
questions.correctAnswer: a limited period when conditions are suitable
questions.explanation: The context uses “window” figuratively for a short opportunity.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: The team tested three paper prototypes. ____ it invited residents to compare them at a public workshop.
questions.correctAnswer: Next,
questions.explanation: The second sentence describes the next step in a sequence.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: The archive had few records from the winter months. ____, researchers used shipping logs to estimate when supplies arrived.
questions.correctAnswer: Nevertheless,
questions.explanation: The second action overcomes the limitation, creating a contrast.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: Which choice most effectively combines the sentences? ‘The observatory opened in 1932. It still hosts public nights.’
options: Opened in 1932, the observatory still hosts public nights.
The observatory opened in 1932, it still hosts public nights.
The observatory opened in 1932 and public nights.
The observatory, opening in 1932, but public nights.
questions.correctAnswer: Opened in 1932, the observatory still hosts public nights.
questions.explanation: The introductory phrase is attached to the observatory and the clause is complete.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: A student wants to emphasize that the method is inexpensive. Which detail best supports that claim?
options: It uses reusable jars collected from local cafés.
It was tested during the spring.
It measures the acidity of soil.
questions.correctAnswer: It uses reusable jars collected from local cafés.
questions.explanation: Reusing locally collected materials directly supports low cost.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: The first model used a single sensor. ____, the revised model uses four sensors to capture readings from different heights.
questions.correctAnswer: By comparison,
questions.explanation: The sentences contrast the two versions.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: A student is writing about a volunteer map project and wants to introduce the map’s purpose. Which sentence best serves that goal?
options: The map helps residents locate repair cafés and tool libraries.
The project meeting lasted about an hour.
The printer was delivered on Tuesday.
questions.correctAnswer: The map helps residents locate repair cafés and tool libraries.
questions.explanation: This sentence states the map’s practical purpose.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: Choose the best transition: ‘The first sample was too small to analyse. ____, the team collected a second sample from a nearby site.’
questions.correctAnswer: Accordingly,
questions.explanation: The collection of a second sample is a response to the problem.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: A student wants to support the claim that a library redesign increased access. Which evidence is strongest?
options: The share of visitors using the step-free entrance rose from 30% to 68%.
The new walls are painted green.
The design committee met on Fridays.
The library has a long history.
questions.correctAnswer: The share of visitors using the step-free entrance rose from 30% to 68%.
questions.explanation: The measured change directly concerns access.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: Which choice most logically completes the text? The seed bank records each sample’s location and collection date. ____.
options: Those records let growers compare varieties under similar conditions.
The building has two exterior doors.
questions.correctAnswer: Those records let growers compare varieties under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Traceable origins make meaningful comparison possible.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: Choose the best transition: ‘The clock’s face was restored. ____, its original brass hands were kept in storage for conservation.’
questions.correctAnswer: However,
questions.explanation: Keeping the hands in storage contrasts with restoring the face.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: Which sentence best concludes a paragraph arguing for shaded waiting areas at bus stops?
options: Shade can make routine waits safer and more comfortable during hot weather.
The bus route has nine stops.
The shelter panels were delivered in May.
questions.correctAnswer: Shade can make routine waits safer and more comfortable during hot weather.
questions.explanation: It synthesizes the reason for the proposed improvement.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: A student wants to compare two survey results. Which transition best completes the sentence? ‘In the first district, 42% of residents walked to the market; ____, 61% did so in the second district.’
questions.correctAnswer: by contrast,
questions.explanation: The sentence compares different percentages across districts.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: Which choice most effectively combines the sentences? ‘The sculpture is made from reclaimed steel. It was designed by Amina Noor.’
options: Designed by Amina Noor, the sculpture is made from reclaimed steel.
The sculpture is made from reclaimed steel, designed by Amina Noor it.
Amina Noor designed and steel reclaimed the sculpture.
The sculpture, and Amina Noor, is made from steel.
questions.correctAnswer: Designed by Amina Noor, the sculpture is made from reclaimed steel.
questions.explanation: The introductory modifier correctly describes the sculpture.

questions.satSkill: Transitions and rhetorical synthesis
questions.text: A student is explaining why a field survey took place at dawn. Which detail is most relevant?
options: The target moths are most active before sunrise.
The route crossed a gravel path.
questions.correctAnswer: The target moths are most active before sunrise.
questions.explanation: The activity pattern explains the survey timing.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The collection of maps, along with two field notebooks, ____ in the archive.
questions.correctAnswer: is
questions.explanation: The singular subject “collection” takes “is”; the intervening phrase does not change agreement.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The engineers revised the plan ____ the first trial revealed a drainage problem.
questions.correctAnswer: because
questions.explanation: The second clause gives the reason for the revision.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: Which choice correctly punctuates the sentence? ‘The device records temperature ____ the notebook records humidity.’
questions.correctAnswer: temperature; the notebook
questions.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: Each of the three proposals ____ a different route through the garden.
questions.correctAnswer: suggests
questions.explanation: “Each” is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The curator displayed the letters, ____ had been found in a sealed desk.
questions.correctAnswer: which
questions.explanation: “Which” introduces a nonessential relative clause after a comma.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The seedlings were moved indoors ____ the overnight temperature was expected to fall below freezing.
questions.correctAnswer: because
questions.explanation: The temperature forecast is the reason for moving the seedlings.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: Which choice uses the apostrophe correctly?
options: The artists studio faces the courtyard.
The artist's studio faces the courtyard.
The artists' studio's faces the courtyard.
The artists studio's face the courtyard.
questions.correctAnswer: The artist's studio faces the courtyard.
questions.explanation: The singular possessive “artist’s” shows ownership.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The route is shorter than ____ used by the earlier survey team.
questions.correctAnswer: the one
questions.explanation: “The one” refers to a singular route.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? ‘After comparing the two samples, ____.’
options: the difference was recorded by the researcher
a difference appeared in the notebook
questions.correctAnswer: the researcher recorded the difference
questions.explanation: The introductory phrase must modify the researcher who compared the samples.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The lights were switched off ____ the presentation had ended.
questions.correctAnswer: after
questions.explanation: “After” clearly expresses the sequence of events.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: Neither the field notes nor the map ____ the footpath’s new name.
questions.correctAnswer: includes
questions.explanation: With “neither…nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer singular subject “map.”

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: Which choice correctly punctuates the introductory phrase?
options: Before the exhibition opened visitors, tested the audio guide.
Before the exhibition opened, visitors tested the audio guide.
Before, the exhibition opened visitors tested the audio guide.
Before the exhibition, opened visitors tested the audio guide.
questions.correctAnswer: Before the exhibition opened, visitors tested the audio guide.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory dependent clause.

questions.satSkill: Boundaries, form, and sentence structure
questions.text: The observatory’s new lens, unlike the older one, ____ images with less distortion.
questions.correctAnswer: produces
questions.explanation: The singular subject “lens” takes “produces.”
